key_insight: HVAF-sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr offered the best combined wear and corrosion performance, while HVOF produced the highest measured hardness.
engineering_relevance: HVAF is a promising coating process for 304 stainless steel components requiring both sliding-wear protection and corrosion resistance.
method: Deposited WC-10Co-4Cr on 304 stainless steel using APS, detonation spraying, HVOF and HVAF.
Compared microstructure, Vickers hardness, sliding wear, friction and corrosion behavior.
Examined wear tracks to identify abrasive and fatigue wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: HVAF achieved a wear rate of (1.10±0.01)×10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), versus (36.82±0.80)×10⁻⁵ for uncoated steel, and the lowest coating corrosion current density at (1.75±0.02) µA/cm².
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or corrosion medium, limiting direct transfer of the rankings to service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
